subject: Timebox pricing: bucket top-up vs prepay structure for BrightLane
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.ch@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@brightlane.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Timebox pricing: bucket top-up vs prepay structure for BrightLane

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our convo with your ML and infra teams, I pulled together two ways customers typically run a 4–6 week timebox evaluation with Redwood:

1) Bucket top-up (recommended for bursty experimentation)
   - You pre-buy a token/compute bucket that acts like a credit pool.
   - We apply automatic top-ups when threshold is hit; unused credits expire at the timebox end.
   - Minimal setup changes; easier to monitor token consumption in Console.

2) Prepay commitment (recommended if you want unit pricing predictability)
   - Prepay for a fixed capacity at a discounted per-token rate.
   - Can include a short runway extension credit if you convert to a committed Dedicated plan.

I've attached a simple pricing sheet with sample numbers for a 4-week pilot and a 6-week stretch, plus an SOW stub for the evaluation scope. Quick notes on options we can flex: smaller incremental buckets, a 30–45 day extension credit if you convert, and invoicing terms.

What matters most for you: absolute unit price or cash flow flexibility? If you tell me that, I can mark up the sheet with a counter we can run by finance/legal.

Next step: if you want, I can schedule a 20-min pricing walkthrough with Marissa (she's cc'd) to run through the tradeoffs and confirm procurement needs.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
irene.ch@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0148

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@brightlane.ai>

Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Timebox pricing: bucket top-up vs prepay structure for BrightLane

Thanks, Irene — helpful summary. A few clarifying questions from our side:

- Our infra team prefers not to prepay large sums up front. Is there a smaller minimum bucket we can start with (e.g., a 1–2 week bucket) and then top-up weekly?
- If we go prepay, procurement will ask for NET-45 or NET-60 invoicing rather than card-on-file. Is that possible for a pilot?
- What SLA (uptime/latency) do we get under the timebox? We need to ensure demo stability for a customer meeting in week 3.

If helpful I can loop in our legal or procurement folks now — procurement@brightlane.ai is cc'd.

Appreciate the quick follow-up. Can your pricing walkthrough cover invoice terms?

Best,
Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Timebox pricing: bucket top-up vs prepay structure for BrightLane

Hi Alex —

Quick answers and a suggested path forward.

1) Minimum bucket: We can do an initial 2-week bucket as a pilot minimum (the XLSX shows a 4-week example; I updated tab "mini-bucket" for a 2-week start). The top-up cadence can be weekly with thresholds at 40%/20% left.

2) Invoicing: For pilots we usually accept card-on-file for speed, but we can offer NET-45 invoicing if procurement signs the pilot SOW and we get an internal PO. I'll attach a short invoice-terms template we send to procurement.

3) SLA: For hosted evaluations we guarantee platform availability aligned with our hosted tier (99.5% monthly), and we can add a higher-priority support channel for the demo window. If you need a formal SLA addendum for the pilot, we can include a one-page exhibit in the SOW.

Discounts / structure: If BrightLane pre-pays a 4-week bucket up front we can offer a 12% prepay discount off list. For the 2-week mini-bucket (weekly top-up), discount is 6%. We can also offer a one-time 5% conversion credit if you convert to Redwood Dedicated within 60 days of the pilot end.

I've attached the updated pricing XLSX and the SOW stub (v1). If this looks OK, Irene and I can run a 20-min call later today or tomorrow to lock the final numbers and invoicing path.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

Marissa / Irene —

Appreciate the options. Procurement did a quick look and asked whether you can do the following so we can get internal approval this week:

- Commit to a 4-week prepay at a 15% discount (your note was 12%);
- Accept NET-60 (not NET-45) for the pilot invoice; and
- Include the 5% conversion credit you mentioned, stacked on top of the prepay discount.

If you can confirm those three items, I'll route the SOW to legal and procurement and we should be able to sign within 5 business days. If NET-60 isn't possible, call out what you can do and we'll try to bridge it.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this spun up next week.

Best,
